questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to try experiencing what it's like to live in a really big city - and preferably in an English-speaking location. I visited Toronto once and thought it seemed like a really cool place. The university also has a great reputation and they offered some really cool courses within my field.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a great experience, and I would highly recommend going on exchange in Toronto!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy to find information regarding academics and we were sent a few emails explaining everything we needed to do. There was no planned orientation for exchange students (besides an informational zoom session) and we were not informed about any regular orientation events at the university which was a bit disappointing.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think they could arrange more social/orientation events for exchange students - it was difficult to meet other exchange students if you did not live in a student residence.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The university does not guarantee on-campus housing for exchange students. Most off-campus student residences (kollegier) only take students that are staying for a full academic year - Tartu College, Campus Co-op, and Hoem on Jarvis are the only ones (I could find) that would let you stay for only 4 months. Tartu and Campus Co-op are quite impossible to get a place at - I applied for Tartu College 2 minutes after they opened for their applications and I still did not get a spot (they distribute rooms based on a first-come basis) - so you have to be really fast/lucky to get a spot there. I ended up staying at Hoem on Jarvis which I would definitely recommend if you want to meet other exchange students, but it is incredibly expensive. Otherwise you can find housing via Airbnb as well.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is very expensive and watch out for scams.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Prioritize living in central Toronto even if it is more expensive than some of the outer areas (York, Scarborough etc.). It is 100 percent worth it - Toronto is a cool city! Public transport also does not really work very well at night, so it is a bit hard to get home if you live far away.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You just had to fill out a Google Form for each course you wanted to register for. Be sure to write the names of your courses in the course prerequisites field in the form. Although they receive a description of all of the courses you have previously taken, it's as if they forget this document exists once you have to apply. I was denied a course because I did not fill it out (because I assumed they had a list of my old courses) - when I applied a second time and filled it out they approved me on the course.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could email the inbound exchange office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all of the classes I applied for - but I was on a waitlist for one of them until 2 days before classes started.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get pre-approval of your courses as early as possible, and get it for many courses so you have the option to switch around if you end up not liking it. If you are on the waitlist you will most likely still get into the class - a lot of students "shop around" and try out a bunch of courses at the start, and then drop out of them.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academics at the University of Toronto were great.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I originally applied to be enrolled in the Graduate School, but for my specific area they did not take exchange students, so I ended up being enrolled as an Undergraduate. I took 3rd and 4th year (level 300 and 400) courses and it was pretty similar in level to UCPH - maybe a bit lower level (but I think this depends on the course).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
At the University of Toronto your final grade depends on many aspects (and not just the final exam). This includes getting graded for presentations, midterms, assignments/essays, and your final exam. This means that there is a bigger workload (because you have more deadlines than at UCPH), but I would say it takes some of the stress away from the exam period. 
The style of teaching is pretty similar to the one at UCPH. My classes only had lectures (no tutorials/practical classes).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
HMB300 - Neurobiology of Behaviour
HMB303 - Global Health and Human Rights
PCL482 - Biomedical Toxicology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: HMB303 - Global Health and Human Rights was a course that was super interesting! It covered a lot of aspects of Global Health and Politics. It was really cool to get a different perspective on science and health care. It is definitely very different from all the other courses I have had during university, but it taught me a lot. The workload is quite intense (you have to submit 7 essays during the semester, and do a presentation - but no exam), but I would still recommend it. The teacher was really excellent and we had some great discussions. I would also recommend the other 2, but they did not really stand out to me specifically.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Rent was very expensive (but this was expected). Everything in Toronto is expensive, especially groceries!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Drinks out could sometimes be cheaper than in DK. Everywhere you would have to add taxes and tips on top of the price, so most things ended up being similar to Danish prices or more expensive. Fast food is less expensive than in DK.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are a ton of non-academic opportunities (clubs, events, sports etc.).

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Clubs of any kind, tons of sports (free gym and workout classes).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the Outdoor Club! They arrange fun events where you get to see some nature close to the city. Many exchange students also join the outdoor club, so it is a good opportunity to meet other exchange students. I also very much utilised the free gym, pool, and workout classes.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Travel around! I went to Montreal, Nova Scotia, and New York - but there are many other cool places to go (Vancouver, Miami, Cuba, Chicago, Algonquin National Park). It's nice to get out of the city every now and then and people are often down to join!
Otherwise I definitely recommend going to see a sport event (at the University it's free, but it's also a great experience to see a real NHL match!). 
Kensington Market is a great area, and Toronto has thousands of cute coffee shops. 
Go to the bar "2 Cats" on Thursdays - they have a great happy hour deal, and you might run into Shawn Mendes ;)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was quite easy - Canada is pretty similar to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It was a bit difficult to socialise with the local students - they are often quite young, and since UofT is quite academically rigororous a lot of them seem to not be super interested in socializing/meeting new people. But I would recommend just speaking to whoever you sit next to in class - due to the way their teaching is structured they most likely also do not know anyone in their class, and it is nice to have a friendly face you can chat with before class starts.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I can't really think of any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Toronto is very diverse which was cool to experience!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I think it is important to take it slow and not put too much pressure on yourself to make your exchange "the best time of your life". Figure out what you enjoy to do and there is no need to feel like you have to be doing something cool or go out at all times - the experience of moving somewhere completely new and having to adapt to a new life is a great experience in itself. Try to not focus that much on school (it can be easy to be stressed out because it is quite an academically intense environment at UofT) - but you will definitely pass your classes! Prioritise going on trips and meeting new people! Bring a winter jacket and buy Uniqlo Heattech ;) - it will get cold.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Phone plans are ridiculously expensive in Canada. I recommend using CBB World (but you need to get a SIM-card and activate it while you're still in DK). Apply for scholarships or take an SU loan - Toronto is expensive and you might as well get the best out of it while you're there instead of stressing out about money.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting all the lovely people from all around the world (and also meeting all the other Danes). It was nice to focus on socialising and experiencing the neighbourhood, instead of worrying about grades or work and other responsibilities at home in DK.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being on your own in a foreign country - it is a challenge, but it is very empowering!

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No :)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
